Part 2 of the diff (pull request) generated, with code changes</figcaption></figure></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>Uber is a good case for learning how much of internal developer infra needs to be rebuilt in order to work well with AI agents.</span></strong><span> Uber built all the tools above because they needed new, better ways to integrate AI agents into the developer workflow, but couldn’t find anything that worked up to requirements. I’d also point out how much time and effort Uber invested in making code review more efficient. Devs are, indeed, getting overloaded with AI code reviews and Uber’s Code Inbox tries to separate the </span><em><span>important</span></em><span> pieces of code to review from </span><em><span>unimportant</span></em><span> ones.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>Startups are jumping into using AI agents, although their integrations are more basic. </span></strong><span>In preparation for the keynote, I talked with several startups about their AI usage. Harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and others are popular, and I also noticed most startups are heavily integrating AI agents into Slack, so devs can kick off bugfixes or small feature requests straight from the chat tool.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>I observed startups being the most likely to experiment with new AI dev tools; from code review, all the way to AI incident management tools.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span>“Traditional” companies are also heavily investing in AI dev tools. </span></strong><span>At the recent Pragmatic Summit in San Francisco, Laura Tacho </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/944ba9c8-9257-48e0-9896-e1ec4501a236?j=eyJ1IjoiMzZ4bDFvIn0.YQmyE28ZLdSE7AAsuvKXIbV3t_oMMHyypLc7Hwjh0tE" style="color: rgb(54,55,55);text-decoration: underline;"><span>shared</span></a><span> interesting details:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span>In February, 18,000 Cisco developers used Codex for complex migrations, code review, and refactoring. This was </span><em><span>very</span></em><span> early – Codex was just starting to gain industry-wide adoption!</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span>JP Morgan Chase built a multi-agent framework for annotation, using multiple specialized agents to label customer interaction data, and judge agents to aggregate and rank results. These are pretty advanced use cases!</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>In general, “traditional” companies do not seem to be lagging behind in using, paying for, and adopting AI agents and AI developer tools.</span></p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span>4. Andi Roberts

item.title: Growing As An Engineer In A World Of AI
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Growing As An Engineer In A World Of AI

Norberto Lopes

“There’s a lot of buzz that AI means companies only want seniors now. That there’s no room left for early career engineers. I don’t think that’s true. The thing actually worth worrying about isn’t whether you’ll get hired, it’s whether you keep learning in a world of AI, now that it removes the friction where that learning used to happen. And that, thankfully, is a choice you get to make.”

#AI CareerGrowth

Ruurtjan Pul

item.title: Our Collective Bike Shed Moment
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Our Collective Bike Shed Moment

Murat Demirbas

“In 1957, Parkinson postulated his "Law of Triviality" using a fictitious committee reviewing plans for a nuclear power plant. The reactor design gets 10 minutes because nobody understands it, so nobody argues. The bike shed gets 45 minutes because everyone has opinions about the paint color. I feel like we are living this committee meeting at scale every day.”

#IndustryTrends
item.description: Our Collective Bike Shed Moment

calc(2em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The Great Restructuring</span></h1><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">AI-native leadership is the most significant organizational transformation since the industry moved to agile more than a decade ago. Several companies watched AI-generated code climb from zero to 50 or 60% of their output inside a single year. Select teams have posted 2 to 10x productivity gains.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">But we keep learning the hard way: individual tool usage produces individual gains, while systemic improvement takes deliberate leadership and a redesign of how work flows.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The evidence is hard to argue with. Around 70% of transformation success comes from operational and cultural change rather than from deploying technology. And most organizations get this wrong. They distribute tools, measure adoption rates, and then wonder why velocity refuses to move.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">But some organizations are getting real results. At Shopify, CEO Tobi Lutke told employees that AI usage is now a baseline expectation, and that teams have to show why a task cannot be done by AI before they ask for more headcount. At Klarna, AI-driven restructuring reduced the workforce by more than a thousand people. These organizations treat AI as a fundamental operating model change, not a tooling upgrade. Almost everyone else is now racing to catch up.</span></p><h1 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(2em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Podified Organizational Structure</span></h1><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">This is the atomic unit of AI-native engineering is the small, cross-functional team: 3 to 5 people operating autonomously with AI agents and tools. The hierarchies established during the dot-com era, all those layers of managers, leads, and coordinators, are being dismantled.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">When a 10x engineer armed with AI tools can do what used to take a much larger group, the organizational consequences are significant. Some pods now report directly to senior leaders based on strategic importance. Team impact gets redefined around outcomes rather than headcount.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The results from one established team’s pod pilot were striking: 3 projects running on self-sufficient agentic loops, more than 90% engineer adoption across the org in under two months, and features built in hours rather than days using agent-assisted development loops.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Roles become fluid in this setup. Engineers may design, designers may code, and product managers may prototype directly. This is not role confusion, it is capability amplification. AI removes the traditional skill bottlenecks, so teams operate with more judgment and less procedural overhead.</span></p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: Resist arbitrary rollout timelines.</span></p></li></ul><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The Agent Champion Model</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Every pillar should name 1 or 2 full-time Agent Champions, responsible for reshaping workflows, preparing codebases, and restructuring operating models. This is not a side-of-desk assignment. It calls for dedicated, high-agency technical leaders who spend 50 to 100% of their time on the transformation itself.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The Champion model reaches well beyond traditional engineering:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: experiment workflows, and cross-functional handoffs for autonomous execution.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Design champions</span></em><span infrastructure.</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">One important note: engineers working with Agent Champions write 70%+ of their code with AI assistance, shifting from human-in-the-loop to human-on-the-loop. The implication is that when those engineers make manual edits, it signals missing AI context rather than business as usual.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Four things matter the most for anyone stepping into the Champion role:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Lead with personal AI adoption first: use the tools daily and share what happens, the wins and the failures alike.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Commit to the vision of AI as foundational to strategy, not an optional enhancement.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Remove barriers through structured, individualized engagement with each team.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Recognize impact based on productivity gains and business outcomes, never on tool usage metrics.</span></p></li></ul><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Leadership Competency Evolution</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Senior leaders are spinning up “AI-native managers” and “AI-native leaders” groups that go deep on the operating context: </span><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">processes</span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">, </span><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">tools</span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">, </span><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">reporting</span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">, and </span><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">metrics</span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">. This is a competency evolution that educational institutions simply cannot keep pace with yet and hence, the need for such learning and development groups at most organizations.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The leadership competency shifts from delegation to orchestration. You are managing multiple parallel AI workflows, not assigning tasks to humans. Technical depth becomes non-negotiable. Hands-on managers have to evaluate agent-generated code and stand up verification layers. And context engineering becomes a core leadership skill, because the precision of the guidance you give AI systems is the precision your teams inherit.</span></p><h1 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(2em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">AI-Native Leadership Crisis From the First Principles</span></h1><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Before we go any deeper into the playbook, it is worth stepping back to the core crisis underneath it all.</span></p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The Bottleneck Was Never Building</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">This is the insight most organizations miss. The dominant narrative celebrates AI’s speed: solo founders shipping with agents, dramatic productivity claims, demos everywhere. But the parts of software development that were always hard, remain hard:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Deciding what to build among competing options</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Identifying the features users actually need</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Prioritizing the capabilities customers will pay for</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Knowing when to kill a project that lacks clear feedback</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Have you heard that building great software is an act of empathy? AI cannot replicate a human understanding of user friction or the emotional stakes inside a product decision. Multiple Y Combinator partners have made the same argument: </span><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">product taste</span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">, </span><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">design sensibility</span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">, and </span><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">customer empathy</span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> become the differentiating human skills once execution is commoditized.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The danger shows up when cheap coding invites excessive feature creation. Users do not get 10x more cognitive bandwidth just because you can ship 10x more features. Teams spiral into uncontrolled development and manufacture false progress.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The shift that matters is asking whether something should be built at all rather than asking if it can be built faster.</span></p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The Ownership Problem</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Anecdotally, most dysfunction in AI-native organizations comes from unclear ownership, not bad process. Even the most empowered teams get fuzzy when responsibility is ambiguous. Work gets picked up or dropped based on whatever is most urgent that day. Leadership becomes the escalation path for every decision, which hollows out middle management and triggers the great flattening.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Piling on more processes to fix a process failure only deepens the hole. The principle is that if something is important enough, give it to a single owner and make them accountable for the outcome.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">We put this into practice with a “STO for Everything” model, where STO stands for Single Task Owner. Each one carries clear priority, authority, and decision rights. This single change turbocharged our transformation by eliminating the coordination tax that ambiguous responsibility almost always creates.</span></p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Why AI Amplifies Ownership Problems</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Because, AI dramatically expands the surface area of parallel work. More projects in flight means more coordination overhead, which triggers an instinct to add process. When ownership stays undefined, those ad hoc processes become bureaucratic substitutes for accountability, and you end up in a vicious cycle.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">You can automate coordination with agents (dependency tracking, scheduling, status summaries), but that only buys temporary relief. It masks the underlying challenges that nobody owns. The moment key people leave, those challenges surface and the systems collapse.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">If you want to fix it, you must  own the outcome, not the process. Map the STO model onto the human-on-the-loop paradigm: </span><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">humans set direction, verify outcomes, and make irreducible judgments, while AI handles the mechanics of execution.</span></em></p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">We Keep Making the Wrong Thing Better</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The most common failure I have watched play out is that teams spend months perfecting products that have no product-market fit. They polish the UI, add settings, refine the copy, all of it generating false progress without changing the trajectory. AI makes this temptation worse by dropping build costs to hours, proliferation of code now drives unvetted product frenzy</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The discipline is to test the hypothesis before committing to development. Ask “What is the scrappiest way to learn whether this matters?” before you build anything. The rapid prototyping ecosystem (Vercel’s v0, Replit Agent, Lovable, Bolt.new) makes that nearly costless.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Then design to 50-60%. Ship the minimal functionality that enables the core user journeys. Watch where users hesitate, misunderstand, or abandon. That tells you the real product challenges instead of the imagined ones. Over 70% of features never reach a real user. In the age of AI, there is no excuse for building fully polished features that nobody wants.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The temptation is real, but giving into it may decide the winner vs. loser product.</span></p><h1 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(2em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Human-Agent Collaboration: The First Step To Tackle the Crisis</span></h1><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The Council of Agents</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Power users have moved past simple human-AI pairing and into orchestrating multiple specialized AI systems that effectively set up a council of agents. There are few different modalities these councils can take.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Role-based delegation treats agents as specialized staff, each with a distinct persona. Cross-evaluation systems deploy multiple agents to independently analyze a problem and review each other’s work. Assembly line workflows chain sequential specialization: architect, then designer, then coder, then reviewer.</span></p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: The key distinction is that agents drive the actual tasks, and humans step in when agents hit an obstacle, not the other way around.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">A few touchpoints make this collaboration work. Every AI module ships with context files that carry a clear architecture context. Work breaks into small, manageable, verifiable chunks. Quality assurance never assumes the AI got it right. And multi-agent coordination manages the interactions between specialized agents.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Teams running AI-first approach often report 2 to 10x acceleration across a wide range of tasks, conditional on getting the foundations right first.</span></p><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">From Human-in-the-Loop to Human-on-the-Loop</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Until 2025, humans had to drive agents hands-on. This year, AI agents have advanced enough so that humans no longer need to sit in the driver’s seat. AI agents self-drive while humans provide oversight, governance, and stay in the loop.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">One large team made the shift cleanly. Humans set the plans and success criteria, AI executes the implementation and self-verifies, AI iterates on its own until the criteria are met, and humans review and approve the final output. This semi-autonomous approach delivered a 40 to 50% speedup over their previous development loop.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The other results have been just as compelling.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">One team’s “Squad of AI Agents” approach drove revenue impact that used to be barely a P25 goal. Another rolled out AI-native workflows targeting 2X-plus productivity, with agents autonomously managing code from authoring through production. A third adopted AI-driven tech debt reduction and gained more than 60% productivity with no quality regression, moving to human-on-the-loop in under 4 months, a transition that usually takes 6 to 12.</span></p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;margin: 32px auto;"><figure style="width: 100%;margin: 0 auto;"><table class="image-wrapper" style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">AI-First MAU:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> 75% or And measure developer experience (satisfaction, flow state, collaboration effectiveness) right alongside the output metrics.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Quality has to be a core metric, not just a guardrail.</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Watch for “AI slop,” the gradual degradation of a codebase as AI-generated code piles up without adequate review. This is the “nobody’s problem” phenomenon, and it can quietly undermine an entire codebase.</span></p></li></ul><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Transformation Anti-Patterns</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Eight patterns that consistently derail transformation need special attention from every AI-native leader:</span></p><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Tool bolt-on:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> AI tools bolted on without redesigning the workflow, producing minimal impact. This is the most common failure mode.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Review bottleneck:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Traditional review steps become the throughput limit once AI accelerates generation.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Prompt cargo culting:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Teams copy external prompts without context and get poor agent performance. The bottleneck is context engineering skill, not the model.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Metrics gaming:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Teams optimize for agent-generated code percentage or adoption stats instead of outcomes.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Security shortcuts:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Privileged agents deployed without proper audit controls. Some of the resulting production incidents are real and expensive.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Knowledge debt:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Verification and specification fall behind agent-generated work, creating maintainability risk that compounds over time.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Junior pipeline hollowing:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Early-career developer experience degrades when human validation gets outsourced to agents. The “missing rung” talent pipeline problem turns into a long-term sustainability risk.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Meeting creep:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> AI acceleration paradoxically makes room for more frequent syncs with no clear impact. style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Use AI personally every day with measurable goals. Set up cross-functional coordination so the whole end-to-end workflow gets transformed.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Pilot pod formation:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Start with a codebase AI readiness assessment. Form 3 to 5-person cross-functional teams with autonomous operation charters. Aim them at real problems, not toy exercises, so the momentum is genuine.</span></p></li></ul><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Phase 2: Systematic Redesign (the next couple of months)</span></h2><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Workflow transformation: </span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Audit the high-friction manual workflows that are good candidates for AI. Move from human-in-the-loop to human-on-the-loop. Build AI-readable documentation and specification systems that turn tribal knowledge into shared knowledge.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Cultural transformation: </span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Establish psychological safety: MIT research found 83% of leaders believe psychological safety measurably improves AI initiative success. Formalize “AI failure story” sessions. Shift measurement from output to outcome.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Technical foundation: </span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Clear out dead code, technical debt, and documentation debt to improve AI readiness. Implement sandboxing controls, audit mechanisms, and automated security checks. Build the verification layers that autonomous AI operation depends on.</span></p></li></ul><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Phase 3: Structural Evolution (everything after)</span></h2><ul style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Flatten hierarchies:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Remove the coordination layers that slow AI-accelerated work. AI-native builders and AI-native leaders are what you need (consider the STO model).</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Impact-based progression:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Reward leverage and outcomes over team size. Define the success metrics that genuinely matter for your organization, and make AI tools and agents your highest-leverage assets.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;mso-special-format: bullet;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Cross-functional fluency:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Let roles flex as AI removes traditional skill barriers. Break down the walls between product management, design, engineering, data science, and field support, so AI-native builders can move fluidly and accelerate their builds.</span></p></li></ul><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Throughout the process, track the compounding gains that show up beyond the initial productivity bump. Connect AI adoption to strategic business metrics. And hold quality standards rigorously, because velocity without quality is a negative value.</span></p><h1 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(2em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Leadership Assessment: Five Questions That Reveal Your Readiness</span></h1><ol style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Impact scaling:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> If you shipped 10x faster, would users be 10x happier? If not, you may be optimizing the wrong thing.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Empathy depth:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Do you understand your users well enough to delete half the interface? Without empathy, more AI-generated features will not fix products that make users feel incompetent.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Learning velocity:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Are you processing real user behavioral data every week? If not, your bottleneck is cycle time to insight, not cycle time to code.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Ownership clarity</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">: Does every major initiative have a single owner? Ownership problems wearing a process-problem costume only get worse under AI acceleration.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Hypothesis discipline:</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Are you testing theses or building products? If you cannot name the signal that would kill your project, you are committed to something with no user validation behind it.</span></p></li></ol><h1 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(2em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">AI-Native Process Optimization: The Final Leadership Imperative</span></h1><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Here is the counterintuitive truth: AI does not reduce the need for process, it changes what the process is for.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Pre-AI processes coordinated execution among humans. AI compresses execution while raising the cost of deciding what is worth executing. The world now runs on simultaneous builds, parallel experiments, and stacks of prototype iterations. The leadership decisions about what matters, what to cut, and what to double down on become the binding constraint.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Process optimization comes down to three questions:</span></p><ol style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">What are we learning this week? </span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Reward faster, deeper learning across teams.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">What are we killing this week?</span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Actively retire the products and agents that lack genuine value.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Who owns each bet, and what signal would change their mind? </span></em><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">STOs steer on objective signals, not intuition and not AI-generated content.</span></p></li></ol><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Everything else is overhead.</span></p><h1 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(2em * 1);"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">How Do You Want to Lead in the AI-Native Era?</span></h1><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The window for this transformation is narrowing. Organizations that pull it off within the next year will open a 5 to 10x productivity gap over the ones that delay, and that gap will be brutally hard to close as AI-native practices compound.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The organizations that succeed show real advantages in product development velocity, technical innovation capacity, and their ability to attract top talent. The early-mover results (2.4x velocity improvements, 60%-plus AI-generated code, features built in hours instead of days) point to a fundamental capability shift rather than an incremental one. A few closing thoughts.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The scarce resource has shifted.</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> It went from generation and production to orchestration and judgment. When AI generates at near-zero marginal cost, the ability to evaluate quality, set direction, and make the hard calls becomes the bottleneck. Leaders who invest in building AI-native team capability will significantly outperform those who just deploy more agents.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Structural change is mandatory.</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> The productivity paradox is real. Individual gains do not become organizational gains without redesigning the workflows, the measurement systems, and the cultural norms. Remember the famous line, “culture eats strategy for breakfast,” only shines brighter under the AI light. No amount of transformation will save you if the foundations and the structure are not redesigned for the AI-native era.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Risk mitigation is continuous, not a one-time fix.</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);"> Monitor AI-generated code quality and maintainability so technical debt does not accumulate. Address the security risks (prompt injection, memory corruption, access control, audit compliance) through embedded CI/CD checks. Prevent the “missing rung” talent pipeline problem by developing AI-native engineers at every level. And hold on to human values while you embrace AI acceleration, because human capital keeps paying dividends in the AI-native era when it is applied well.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;margin-bottom: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">AI changes the tools. It does not change the core reality. The hard part stays </span><strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">insanely human</span></strong><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, item.title: Banned book library
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
Banned book library

Rick Osgood

34 minutes by Rick Osgood A hacked WiFi smart light bulb can secretly host banned books as a public digital library. The bulb creates an open WiFi access point, and anyone nearby can connect and browse the books through a web browser. The project uses a cheap ESP32 based smart bulb flashed with custom firmware, with storage expanded by repartitioning the 4MB chip. The 4MB limit means only a few books fit, but that turns each bulb into a personal statement about what its creator finds worth preserving. AURI catches the security issues your AI coding agent introduces
item.description: Banned book library

item.title: Six SQL patterns I use to catch transaction fraud
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
Six SQL patterns I use to catch transaction fraud

Fixel Smith

10 minutes by Fixel Smith Fraud detection usually comes down to SQL, not fancy machine learning. Fixel shares six core query patterns which cover most cases: transaction velocity, impossible geographic travel, suspicious amounts, compromised merchants, off-hours activity, and window functions that combine the others. No single pattern is enough on its own, but transactions that fail three or four checks are almost always fraud. Start with velocity, then build from there.
item.description: Six SQL patterns I use to catch transaction fraud

item.title: Stop using Conventional Commits
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
Stop using Conventional Commits

Sumner Evans

9 minutes by Sumner Evans Conventional Commits puts commit type like "fix" or "feat" before scope, but scope is what developers actually need when reading logs. Type is usually obvious from the description anyway. The promised benefits like auto-generated changelogs and version bumping fail in practice because changelogs and commit logs serve different audiences with different needs. Projects like Linux and Git use simple scope-first commit messages and work far better.
item.description: Stop using Conventional Commits

item.title: How 2004 RuneScape fit a multiplayer RPG into 56k dial-up
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
How 2004 RuneScape fit a multiplayer RPG into 56k dial-up

James Monger

26 minutes by James Monger James explains how RuneScape supported thousands of players on slow 56k dial-up connections. Using examples from a decompiled game client, he shows how Jagex minimized network traffic through bit-packing, relative coordinates, compact updates, and shared client-server logic. James also highlights how careful protocol design reduced data transfer while maintaining a large multiplayer world, offering lessons that remain relevant for modern networked systems.
item.description: How 2004 RuneScape fit a multiplayer RPG into 56k dial-up

item.title: Stop using JWTs
item.author: Programming Digest <jakub@programmingdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
Stop using JWTs

Luminessa Starlight

3 minutes by Luminessa Starlight Luminessa argues that JWTs are unsuitable for user authentication sessions because they are designed for short-lived tokens and introduce security and management challenges. She recommends traditional cookie-based sessions as a safer, more efficient solution. For short-lived signed tokens, she suggests using PASETO instead of JWTs. item.description: Stop using JWTs

item.title: publishing
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
publishing

Hamed Salameh

Saving data and publishing a message are two separate operations, so a crash between them can silently lose events. The Outbox Pattern fixes this by writing messages to a database table in the same transaction as your business data, then using a background dispatcher to publish them to the broker. This gives you at-least-once delivery without any distributed coordination. Hamed walks through a full .NET 10 implementation using EF Core, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, and MassTransit. See one of the few solutions purpose-built for generating real
item.description: publishing

item.title: vulnerability reports
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
vulnerability reports

Nikolche Kolev

.NET 10 now removes platform-provided packages from dependency graphs by default. Many libraries pull in packages like System.Text.Json as dependencies even when the .NET runtime already includes a newer version, causing false vulnerability warnings. Package pruning strips these redundant entries at restore time, cutting false-positive vulnerability reports by 70% and reducing restore times by up to 50%.
item.description: vulnerability reports

item.title: EF Core in clean architecture the pragmatic way
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
EF Core in clean architecture the pragmatic way

Anton Martyniuk

Wrapping EF Core in a repository layer adds unnecessary complexity since DbContext already implements those patterns. Using DbContext directly in application use cases keeps code simpler, easier to read, and faster to change. Tests improve too, as running against a real database with tools like Testcontainers catches bugs that mocked repositories miss. Custom repositories still make sense for complex shared queries, multiple data sources, or strict team conventions.
item.description: EF Core in clean architecture the pragmatic way

item.title: New lines are more than \r and \n
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
New lines are more than \r and \n

Gérald Barré

Most developers only think of \r\n and \n as line breaks, but Unicode defines several more, including \u0085, \u2028, and \u2029. Ignoring these can cause parsing bugs when handling text from office tools, legacy systems, or cross-platform sources. In .NET, you can handle all cases using a regex pattern, string.ReplaceLineEndings, or the SplitLines helper from Meziantou.Framework. item.description: New lines are more than \r and \n

item.title: rows without the wait
item.author: C# Digest <jakub@csharpdigest.net>
item.ns0:encoded:
rows without the wait

Chris Woodruff

Inserting large volumes of data with a simple foreach loop works fine locally but falls apart in production due to slow change tracking, too many database round trips, and high memory use. EF Core 10's native AddRange with a single SaveChangesAsync call solves most of this through batching and fixes the change tracker overhead. For higher volumes or complex parent-child data, Entity Framework Extensions adds bulk insert methods that match raw SQL speed while keeping EF Core model integration. 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);">Big models cost more. Small models do less. Here's how SLMs and LLMs differ across the dimensions that matter in production: </span></p><ol style="margin-top: 0;padding: 0;"><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);">Architecture: SLMs are usually under 10B parameters and run on a laptop or phone. LLMs sit at 10B+ with deeper layers and more attention heads, built for broad reasoning across tasks.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);">Task Complexity: SLMs work well on simple tasks but fail on complex multiple reasoning steps. LLMs handle difficult math, multi-step code, and long-horizon planning. </span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);">Long Context Recall: SLMs lose the thread across long documents or extended conversations. LLMs reliably track and connect information across large inputs.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);">Latency and Cost: SLMs run on consumer hardware with low response times and significantly lower inference costs. LLMs require GPU and carry higher costs per request.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);">Deployment and Privacy: SLMs run on-device or on-premise. LLMs are typically cloud-hosted, which adds data governance complexity.</span></p></li><li style="margin: 8px 0 0 32px;"><p style="color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;margin-bottom: 0;box-sizing: border-box;padding-left: 4px;font-size: 16px;margin: 0;"><span data-color="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);"><span>Where each fits:</span><br><span>SLMs: on-device assistants, real-time classification, or privacy-sensitive applications</span><br><span>LLMs: complex reasoning, agent workflows, or broad knowledge tasks.</span></span></p></li></ol><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);"><span>Are you using SLMs, LLMs, or a hybrid setup in production?</span><br></span></p><div style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;"><hr style="margin: 32px 0;padding: 0;height: 1px;background: rgb(0,0,0,.1);border: none;"></div><h2 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.625em * 1);"><span data-color="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);">Single Agent vs. Multi-Agent Architecture</span></h2><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span data-color="rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9)" style="color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.9);">Some tasks need a single agent. item.title: Revised Rules Of Engineering Leadership
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Revised Rules Of Engineering Leadership

Will Larson

“This post documents the new rules I’ve revised my approach to engineering leadership around, and then talks through the specific projects I’ve worked on over the past year that caused me to believe in these rules.”

#Leadership Management
item.description: Revised Rules Of Engineering Leadership

item.title: Don't Stack Weaknesses
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Don't Stack Weaknesses

Yue Zhao

“The real damage happens when you stack weaknesses - when a leader is weak at something and their direct reports are weak at the same thing. This is a disaster, and it happens far more often than you’d think. Part of the reason for this is that leaders tend to hire people with the same skills they have. They’ll dress it up as hiring for “values” instead of “skills” so it doesn’t look like they’re cloning themselves - but people ultimately search for and evaluate the things they’re good at.”

#Management Hiring
item.description: Don't Stack Weaknesses

item.title: Why Spreading Yourself Thin Feels Like Winning
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Why Spreading Yourself Thin Feels Like Winning

Steve Huynh

“Every “yes” is a check written against the future that has to be cleared. And clearing checks written by “powerful Us” is especially tough. Why? Because, by definition, we are only average most of the time. This article provides a guide to recognizing overextension in ourselves, so that, before we commit to things, we can be sure that we are only taking on what we can hold.”

#CareerGrowth DecisionMaking Wellbeing
item.description: Why Spreading Yourself Thin Feels Like Winning

item.title: The Worst Take In Tech: New Grad Hiring
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
The Worst Take In Tech: New Grad Hiring

Scott Kennedy

“In this generation we call them “AI Natives”. The advantage is that there are no old habits to break or reframe. Many experienced folks are open minded and can do it, but many resist. New grads don’t know the difference, their learning came in parallel to having these tools. We see it in interviews regularly, new grads can use AI coding tools incredibly well.”

#IndustryTrends AI Hiring
item.description: The Worst Take In Tech: New Grad Hiring

item.title: Why Is Meta Destroying Its Engineering Organization?
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Why Is Meta Destroying Its Engineering Organization?

Gergely Orosz

“In this article, we walk through what’s happened, and ask what’s going through the minds of leadership who are reducing software engineering there from the profit center that it was between 2004 until very recently, to the disdained cost center that it has become in just a few weeks.”

#IndustryTrends Leadership
item.description: Why Is Meta Destroying Its Engineering Organization?

item.title: SQLite Improving Performance With Pre-Sort
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
SQLite Improving Performance With Pre-Sort

Anders Murphy

“The defining characteristic of a B+ Tree is that it is ordered. Sequential writes are fast. Random data works against this thrashing pages, causing page splits and tree re-balancing. It's not a good time. But, we are batching the data already. So what if we sort it before we insert?”

#Database DeepDive Performance
item.description: SQLite Improving Performance With Pre-Sort

item.title: Agentic Code Review
item.author: Pointer <suraj@pointer.io>
item.ns0:encoded:
Agentic Code Review

Addy Osmani

“Stop reviewing everything to the same depth. Spend scarce human attention only where being wrong is costly, and let cheap deterministic gates and AI reviewers handle the rest. The organizing idea is to match review effort to the cost of being wrong, push the cheap deterministic work as early as possible, and reserve human attention for what only humans can do.”

#CodeReview AI Agents
item.description: Agentic Code Review

20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;margin-top: 0;"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Observability for Beginners: Logs, Metrics, Traces, and Everything Around Them</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">A running service generates events constantly.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Requests arrive, functions run, errors appear, and each one is a thing that happened at a specific time with a specific context and a specific outcome.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Logs, metrics, and traces are three ways of looking at this same stream. A log captures one event as a line of text, a metric counts or aggregates many events, and a trace links related events as they move across services. Most of the concepts in observability, including cardinality, sampling, and correlation, are consequences of this structure.</span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;text-align: justify"><span data-color="rgb(0, 0, 0)" style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">In this article, we will look at the basics of observability in detail with concepts like logs,
